identity.real_world_identity_notes: ORECA specifies the 07 with a six-speed sequential Xtrac gearbox and pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift. AMS2 exposes the same exact model identity in LMP2 and LMP2_Gen1 class contexts. The exact Low Downforce identity is treated as an aero-package alias inheriting the base controls and has not been separately live-tested.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, both AMS2 class generations moved from rest without physical clutch input. The simulator mechanism was not established.
Both generations exposed six paddle-selected forward gears and accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts without driver lift; automatic cut was perceptible.
Both generations accepted clutch-free downshifts with the driver's foot off throttle, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.
The exact Oreca 07 - Low Downforce identity inherits these controls as an approved aero-package assumption. Only the base identity was live-tested.
Gen1 and Gen2 were live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Both contexts confirmed six paddle-selected gears, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with automatic cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and the same closed GT/Formula display rim.
Physical clutch input was not required to move from rest, but the underlying mechanism was not determined.
The Low Downforce identity inherits the base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.

confidence.basis: Exact identities and the full user-facing control technique were directly checked in both AMS2 class generations; the manufacturer independently establishes the gearbox hardware. Low Downforce remains an explicitly noted aero-package inheritance.

claims.basis: Official addition plus exact live model and class observations through SimHub 9.11.22.
Low Downforce is an exact observed identity whose controls are explicitly inherited from the tested base as an aero-package assumption; the variant itself was not live-tested.
Manufacturer specification and direct exercise of all six paddle-selected forward gears agree.
Both class generations directly demonstrated clutch-free move-off, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with perceptible cut, and clutch-free downshifts with a visible automatic-blip throttle spike.
Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display.

notes: One record covers both directly observed AMS2 class contexts because their exact model identity and tested controls are the same.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "prototype", a value that named a racing category rather than a rim outline. That value is retired: the rims it covered are the same closed form, flattened at both the top and the bottom, that the project now records as "gt-style". The shape was remapped by definition and the rim was not observed again.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
